mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwanese investing company (proof of legal existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (company registration authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path: notarization by a Taiwan notary public; authentication by the Taiwan district court or Ministry of Economic Affairs; verification and transmission through the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); final certification by the competent PRC notary or consular/foreign affairs office before submission to SAMR. No Hague Apostille may be used because Taiwan is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; the paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Company Registration Records of the Taiwanese investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, and the Taiwan Corporate Affairs authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path: Taiwan notary public notarization; authentication by the Taiwan district court and Ministry of Economic Affairs; SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification; final certification by a PRC notary or designated consular authentication authority. Apostille is unavailable for Taiwan-origin documents because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention contracting party; no sequential use of both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing the formation of the China WFOE and appointing the legal representative and local managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwanese investing company board of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path if signed in Taiwan: notarization of the directors' signatures by a Taiwan notary; court/MOEA authentication; SEF/ARATS verification; PRC notary or consular legalization. If signed before a PRC notary in mainland China, it may be notarized domestically by a PRC notary office and requires no Apostille or consular legalization for SAMR filing; the selected path must be final and must not be chained with the other path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles) of the proposed China WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders / proposed WFOE legal representative and PRC counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic PRC path: execution before a PRC notary public and submission to SAMR; no Hague Apostille or consular legalization is required for domestic incorporation. If the executed instrument is later used abroad, the paths are alternative: for Hague Apostille member states, PRC notary + local Foreign Affairs Office + Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille; for non-member states, PRC notary + Foreign Affairs Office + destination-state consular legalization. Never combine both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Taiwanese investor's principal relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwanese investor's principal bank (relationship manager / compliance officer)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path: bank officer signature notarized by a Taiwan notary; authentication by the Taiwan court or MOEA; SEF/ARATS verification; final PRC consular/notarial legalization. The bank letter must be current, issued on bank letterhead, signed and sealed by an authorized compliance officer, and must not be apostilled because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention state; the consular path is the sole permissible route.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All direct and indirect shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, supervisors, the legal representative, senior managers, authorized signatories, and bank account users must be screened before name clearance, before incorporation filing, and before any capital contribution. Screening must be run against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and China's domestic AML/CFT blacklists maintained by the People's Bank of China and the Ministry of Public Security. Each subject must also be checked against global politically exposed person (PEP) databases, including family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and an archived written risk assessment. Negative news, adverse media, regulatory enforcement, and shell-company risk indicators must be documented and re-screened at least every 180 days; all records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Independent Declaration and Registration System, accessed through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System online platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE legal name must be in simplified Chinese and must follow the mandatory four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive name (字号) + industry or business characteristics + company type, limited liability company. The distinctive name must contain two or more standard simplified Chinese characters; traditional Chinese characters, Japanese kanji, Arabic numerals, Latin letters, and symbols are not permitted unless separately approved by SAMR. A foreign-language English translation may be used only as an auxiliary convenience name and does not create a separate legal name. Where the Taiwanese parent's name is transliterated, the pinyin romanization standard is used, and the transliteration must not mislead the public, conflict with prior registered names, or infringe existing trademarks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: "Military", "Police", "State Security", and similar government authority terms
"Government", "Authority", and words importing state sponsorship without authorization
"Group" (集团公司) where no qualified group company structure exists
"Foreign" and words implying foreign-state endorsement without ministerial approval
"Taiwan" as part of the trade name unless separately cleared through the applicable cross-strait approval mechanism
"Export", "Import", "Trading", and "E-commerce" where a negative-list industry license or cross-department approval is required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, download and preserve the SAMR name rejection notice identifying the conflicting prior name, prohibited token, or missing approval. Within 60 days from notice, submit a written administrative reconsideration application to the next-higher SAMR authority or the deciding SAMR office under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, attaching the original rejection notice, a legal opinion, a China trademark and trade-name search report, and, where applicable, the prior rights holder's written consent. The reconsideration authority must generally decide within 60 days. If reconsideration fails, file an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months. In parallel, declare a fresh alternative name through the online portal so incorporation is not delayed; the appeal does not suspend the need for a valid name reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox, without any physical presence, lease, management, or on-site records, is generally rejected by SAMR, municipal tax authorities, and bank KYC compliance teams for an Internet retail WFOE because it fails the commercial substance test. The WFOE must maintain a registered address that can receive official mail, store books and records, and support actual management and retail operations. Some licensed address-hosting services in free-trade zones or business incubators may provide a lawful registered address, but only if the provider holds the required administrative license and issues compliant lease and invoice records. Declaring a virtual office will trigger enhanced scrutiny under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 beneficial-owner registration, VAT invoice controls, and corporate bank account opening procedures.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection: (1) exterior and interior signage exactly matching the registered name; (2) original lease agreement and property ownership certificate or licensed address-host agreement; (3) on-site books, contracts, invoices, and ISIC 4791 e-commerce transaction records; (4) legal representative or at least one manager present during working hours; (5) computer systems showing active Internet retailing of outdoor sports and camping gear; (6) utility bills, property fees, payroll records, and inventory/receipts corroborating declared commercial substance. Quantified risk: 65-75% probability of a SAMR or municipal tax inspection within the first 12 months where only a virtual office address is declared; 30-40% where a serviced office with physical signage, daily staffing, and complete records is maintained. For an e-commerce WFOE issuing VAT invoices or remitting cross-border sales proceeds, district tax authorities may require an inspection if annual turnover exceeds approximately RMB 5 million or if payment processing via Stripe, PayPal, or similar rails creates customs and foreign-exchange flags.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, Articles 1, 2, 5, 12, 15, 18, 100, 128, 129, 156, 172, 192, 208, and 387; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Article 7; Investment Commission Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Division, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (unified form under Article 387 of the Taiwan Company Act) submitted through the MOEA Company Registration Online Application System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for a company limited by shares under the current Taiwan Company Act. The Company must, however, have paid-in capital sufficient to support its proposed business scope, and the subscribed capital must be remitted into and held in a Taiwan bank account before registration. No statutory escrow account is required, but a bank deposit certificate or a certified public accountant capital verification report must be submitted with the incorporation filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company, the adoption of the Articles of Incorporation presented to this meeting, and the preliminary corporate actions taken by the incorporators are approved, ratified, and confirmed. The authorized share capital shall be [amount] New Taiwan Dollars, divided into [number] ordinary shares with par value NT$10 each. The initial paid-in capital shall be [amount] New Taiwan Dollars. All subscriptions to such shares are accepted in full, and each shareholder shall pay the contribution in cash or by bank wire transfer to the Company's capital collection account prior to the filing of the Company Registration Application.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office and principal place of business shall be at [full address], Taiwan (R.O.C.), which is adopted as the Company's statutory seat and legal domicile, and where the statutory books and corporate seal shall be maintained. The registered office may be changed only by a subsequent resolution of the Board of Directors and a conforming filing with the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each acting singly, are authorized to open, maintain, operate, and close bank accounts at any financial institution in Taiwan; to execute account opening forms, deposit instructions, wire transfer orders, and loan or guarantee documents within the scope of ordinary business; and to give valid receipts and discharges for all funds received by the Company.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are appointed as the first statutory officers of the Company, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until a successor is elected and qualified: (a) [Name] as Director and Chairman; (b) [Name] as Chief Executive Officer; (c) [Name] as Chief Financial Officer; and (d) [Name] as Corporate Secretary.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairman and Corporate Secretary, together or individually, are authorized to execute and file the Application for Company Registration, the Articles of Incorporation, the foreign investment approval documents, tax registration forms, and all other instruments necessary to establish the Company; to make all statutory declarations; and to amend any document if required by the Registrar. All actions taken by the officers before the date of this resolution in furtherance of incorporation are ratified and confirmed.

This resolution shall be effective immediately upon adoption and shall remain in full force until amended, superseded, or revoked by a duly adopted resolution of the Board of Directors or the Shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the MOEA Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval System with the applicant's digital certificate or foreign passport registration. Submit the proposed English and Chinese company names, the exact business scope description 'Internet retailing of outdoor sports and camping gear', and the intended registered address district. The system will run an automatic conflict check against existing registered names and the list of names that are susceptible to confusion or prohibited by law. After the pre-approval is granted, download the certificate of pre-approval within the validity period, because the reservation lapses if the company registration is not filed before expiration. Ensure the corporate name includes a legal entity suffix such as 'Limited', and do not proceed to bank opening until the pre-approval is obtained.
required_dossiers: Applicant's digital certificate or passport copy
Proposed Chinese and English company names
Precise business scope description
Intended registered office address or district
Power of attorney if filed through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name or scope is rejected, log into the same system and resubmit with amended names or a narrower business scope. A formal written appeal may be filed with the Department of Commercial Affairs within 30 days of the rejection, accompanied by a legal argument that the proposed name is not confusingly similar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment and Inward Remittance Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the Foreign Investment Application with the Investment Commission, MOEA. Attach notarized proof of the foreign investor's identity or corporate existence, bank statements proving available funds, a business plan for the Taiwan operations, and a power of attorney appointing a resident agent. The Investment Commission will verify that the proposed business does not fall within the Negative List for foreign investment. Upon approval, the investor will receive an approval letter that may be presented to a Taiwan bank to open a foreign capital account. The approved capital must be remitted into Taiwan and deposited before the company registration application is filed. Any subsequent change to the investment amount or business scope requires a new approval or an amendment approval.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Notarized investor identity certificate or foreign company registration
Bank balance certificate or proof of funds
Business plan for Taiwan operations
Power of attorney appointing a resident representative
Company name pre-approval certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query, respond with supplemental documentation within 30 days. If the application is denied, the investor may file a petition for administrative reconsideration within 30 days after receipt of the written denial, or submit a revised application with a reduced scope or adjusted investment amount.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Bank in Taiwan and Taiwan Certified Public Accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a company bank account in the provisional corporate name using the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, the draft Articles of Incorporation, and the company name pre-approval certificate. Deposit the full subscribed paid-in capital into the account and obtain a bank deposit certificate or a bank-confirmed capital introduction record. Retain a licensed Taiwan CPA to examine the remittance trail and confirm that the capital is not fictitious or borrowed. The CPA will issue a capital verification report, or the bank may provide a certified deposit statement acceptable to the Registrar. The capital verification report must be dated no earlier than 15 days before the filing of the Company Registration Application. Foreign currency remittances must be converted into New Taiwan Dollars through the banking system and recorded in the Company's capital account.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Company name pre-approval certificate
Bank account opening application and corporate seal specimen
Inward remittance and deposit receipts
CPA capital verification report or bank certified deposit statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening due to incomplete documentation, correct the missing items and resubmit. If the CPA raises a capital substance concern, provide additional source-of-funds evidence or return the remittance and file a revised capital plan. Re-issue the verification report if more than 15 days have passed since its date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration Filing and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, One-Stop Registration Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Company Registration through the One-Stop Registration portal or at the competent district office of the Department of Commercial Affairs. Include the Articles of Incorporation, the First Board Resolution, the CPA capital verification report, the registered office lease or owner-consent document, and copies of the directors' and shareholders' identification. The Registrar will conduct a formal completeness check and legal review of the company name, business scope, director qualifications, and registered office. If all requirements are satisfied, the MOEA will issue the Company Registration Certificate and transmit the basic registration data to the National Taxation Bureau. The standard processing time is five working days, but the application may be suspended if the foreign investment approval letter or capital certificate is missing.
required_dossiers: Application for Company Registration
Articles of Incorporation
First Board of Directors Resolution
CPA capital verification report and bank certificate
Registered office lease, title deed, or owner consent
Passport or ID copies of directors and shareholders
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Company name pre-approval certificate
Company seal or chop specimen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of incompleteness or statutory defect, remediate the identified matter within 30 days and submit a revised filing through the portal. If the company registration is suspended, request a written explanation and file an administrative appeal with the MOEA within 30 days of the suspension notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, and Local Labor/Insurance Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, apply to the National Taxation Bureau branch with local jurisdiction to complete tax registration, uniform invoice assignment, and withholding tax registration. The application must be filed within 15 days after the date of the Company Registration Certificate. Provide the certificate, the business seal, the responsible person's identification, and the registered office evidence. The tax authority will issue a tax registration number and approve the use of uniform invoices if the company is engaged in selling goods or services. The Company must also register as an employer unit with the local labor insurance and health insurance administration in order to hire employees. Only after the tax registration and employer registration are complete may the Company lawfully issue sales invoices and remit employees' social insurance contributions.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Company seal and responsible person ID
Registered office lease or ownership evidence
Tax registration application form
Uniform invoice questionnaire and business premises photos
Employer unit registration form for labor and health insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority questions the business scope or registered office, provide supplementary photographs, lease contracts, or utility bills. If the uniform invoice application is rejected, reapply after correcting the stated business premises or sales model. Late filing penalties may be mitigated by promptly filing an amended application before a formal assessment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or physical retail premise requires an industrial operating license under the current e-commerce retail scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - exempt; no Environmental Impact Assessment is required for pure internet retailing without a physical production facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generating processes are established at this stage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at the registration stage; the Company operates only as an internet retailer with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing site. If a warehouse or fulfillment center is later established in Taiwan, the Company must obtain a Fire Safety Equipment Compliance Certificate from the local fire department and comply with workplace safety registration under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), acting through local provincial and municipal tax service bureaus; the online electronic portal is the National Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax portal) administered by the STA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident investor establishing a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise in Mainland China, the WFOE must: (1) obtain notarized, apostilled or legalized foreign investor documentation and board resolutions; (2) complete foreign investment filing or negative-list review with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and business registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), obtaining the Business License and the Unified Social Credit Code, which functions as the statutory taxpayer identification number for tax, customs, and social insurance; (3) within 30 days of Business License issuance, complete tax registration through the National Electronic Tax Bureau portal by submitting the articles of association, lease or address certificate, investor identity documents, and bank account information; (4) complete VAT taxpayer status election, whether small-scale taxpayer or general taxpayer, based on projected turnover; (5) register separately with the local tax authority for urban construction tax, education surcharges, payroll withholding, and stamp duty; (6) register with the General Administration of Customs for export procedures and with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for foreign-exchange receipts; (7) bind the e-Tax account and receive the electronic tax registration certificate. No separate TIN certificate is issued beyond the Unified Social Credit Code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for pass-through or hybrid mismatch elections: a Chinese WFOE is mandatorily subject to entity-level taxation under the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China. However, the enterprise may elect between small-scale VAT taxpayer status and general VAT taxpayer status when annual taxable turnover is below RMB 5,000,000, and may elect simplified tax collection methods where statutory conditions are met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales, being the mandatory turnover threshold for registration as a general VAT taxpayer; basic tax and VAT registration is required for all formed entities within 30 days of Business License issuance, irrespective of actual turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory digital invoicing under the Golden Tax Phase IV framework: VAT invoices must be issued through the STA's Electronic Tax Bureau platform or certified API integrations, and invoice data must be transmitted in real time to the STA. Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoices carry encrypted tax-control codes and digital signatures that serve as the anti-fraud stamp; no manual physical stamping is required once the invoice is issued and cleared through the national electronic invoice system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Chinese VAT general taxpayer may claim zero-rate, being exemption with credit or refund, for outdoor camping equipment exported from the Mainland customs territory, including deliveries to Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau, provided: the goods are physically exported and cleared by Mainland customs under an export declaration; the exporter maintains complete input VAT documentation; the goods are not on the export prohibition or restriction list; export sales are evidenced by commercial contracts, customs declarations, and logistics documents; and export proceeds are repatriated and settled in accordance with SAFE requirements. Cross-border e-commerce retail export goods may also qualify when order, payment, and logistics data are transmitted electronically through the China International Single Window. Qualifying offshore and digital services supplied to overseas recipients and wholly consumed outside Mainland China may also be zero-rated or exempt under the cross-border services negative list.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Form (export goods declaration submitted through the China International Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the Mainland customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or SAFE banking foreign-exchange receipt record evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Export sales contract or customer purchase order
VAT invoice (export version) or cross-border e-commerce export declaration data in the customs unified system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to joint audit by the STA, General Administration of Customs, and SAFE, using Golden Tax IV data matching, customs declaration comparison, logistics trail verification, and foreign-exchange archive checks. Missing or inconsistent substantiation results in denial or clawback of VAT exemption or refund amounts plus statutory late-payment surcharges and interest. Fraudulent claims, including forged customs declarations, false bills of lading, phantom exporters, circular foreign-exchange arrangements, or fake invoices, attract administrative fines, tax-credit blacklisting and heightened risk-monitoring status, revocation of VAT refund qualifications, and criminal prosecution for fraudulent export tax-refund claims under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed foreign exchange system under PBOC/SAFE. The current account has attained factual convertibility: cross-border trade in goods and services, including export collections and payment of trade-related fees, can be settled through designated banks against verifiable commercial documents. The capital account remains tightly controlled, and every cross-border capital event — inbound direct investment, foreign borrowings, profit repatriation, share transfer, or liquidation — must be registered and approved or recorded by SAFE. For a Taiwan-owned WFOE, foreign exchange capital remitted into the registered capital account cannot be used at will; it must be converted into RMB only within the scope permitted by the FDI settlement rules and cannot be used for working capital outside the declaration. Profit remittance by the WFOE to the Taiwan parent requires audited financial statements, tax payment certification, and a SAFE-controlled foreign exchange payment, but there is no quarantine surcharge. Export receipts are no longer subject to mandatory surrender; however, they must be repatriated into China and reported to SAFE through the goods trade monitoring system. Offshore NDF arrangements for CNY are not an onshore corporate solution, and all hedging must be genuine-demand based at licensed domestic banks. This dual-track structure necessitates treasury planning that segregates current account flows from capital account flows at every transaction level.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to China and credited to the enterprise's current account foreign exchange settlement account within the normal trade settlement cycle; there is no statutory mandatory conversion percentage, and the WFOE may retain 100% of export receipts in foreign currency or voluntarily convert them into RMB through a designated forex bank. The bank must report each receipt or payment to SAFE under the trade-in-goods monitoring system within 30 days, presenting the customs declaration, invoice, and logistic evidence supporting the underlying transaction.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for offshore digital EMI platforms. A mainland China WFOE is not eligible to open a primary settlement account with overseas fintech EMIs such as U.K., Singapore, or Hong Kong e-money institutions, because those entities are not licensed by PBOC/SAFE to operate in mainland China and cannot deliver onshore CNY clearing or compliant SAFE reporting. Stripe does not directly onboard mainland China incorporated entities, while PayPal China holds a non-bank payment license and may be used only as a downstream e-commerce collection channel; the final corporate treasury and FX clearing must still sit with a licensed domestic bank. Fintech EMIs should therefore be positioned only as supplementary merchant collection aggregators, never as the regulated banking rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance of the legal representative and at least one statutory director is generally mandatory for initial account opening at Tier-1 Chinese banks. Remote consular proxy opening is not a recognized replacement for WFOE onboarding. Where a Taiwan-based legal representative cannot travel, the bank may accept a written power of attorney issued to an onshore authorized person, provided the POA is notarized in Taiwan and authenticated through the cross-strait notarization and authentication channel, and the bank completes a recorded video interview with the legal representative and performs enhanced due diligence on the Taiwan corporate registry and investment approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwan top shareholder structure is an opacity flag — a holding company with no audited financials or office, making the true beneficial owner unverified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate registry from Taiwan reflecting the full shareholder chain, audited financial statements of each intermediate holding entity, beneficial ownership declaration signed by the ultimate Taiwan individual, board resolution authorizing the WFOE establishment, passport or ID copies, proof of business address, and a cross-strait authenticated certificate of corporate registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound paid-in capital arrives from a Hong Kong or Singapore intermediary account instead of the named Taiwan investor, triggering source-of-funds and round-tripping suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Taiwan investment commission approval letter for mainland China investment, the board resolution fixing the remittance route, the signed investment agreement, the full SWIFT MT103 chain showing beneficial ownership of funds, source-of-wealth documentation for the Taiwan investor, bank statements for the prior 12 months, and a written explanation of any third-country funding conduit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export revenue from outdoor camping gear received via Stripe or PayPal aggregator accounts shows remitter names that do not match the end retail customers, which looks like split payment or disguised commercial payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce platform payout reports, the payment processor merchant agreement, order-level reconciliation ledger matching each payout to unique customer orders, customs export declarations, logistics waybills, refund and chargeback records, the WFOE's sales contracts, and the bank statement of the settlement account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid alternation between the RMB settlement account and the FX capital account to pay mainland suppliers or individuals is detected as an attempt to bypass SAFE current and capital account separation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration and capital account transaction record, current account invoice package containing contract, invoice, customs forms and logistics evidence, related-party transfer pricing documentation, supplier and customer KYB files, board-approved cash flow forecast, and a statutory auditor's confirmation that no capital account funds were used for prohibited current expenditures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must obtain the applicable investment approval and the China WFOE must complete SAFE FDI registration before any funds are sent. The efficient clearing route is a single SWIFT remittance in USD or HKD from the Taiwan shareholder to the WFOE's designated FDI foreign exchange capital account at a Tier-1 bank, with the purpose coded as direct investment equity capital injection. Upon receipt, the bank matches the remittance to the SAFE FDI record and capital verification reference; funds can be converted into RMB through settlement against the capital account, and a China-certified public accountant issues the capital verification report. No inward wire should reference the e-commerce business as trade payment, because that would misclassify capital account money as current account inflows and trigger rejection or SAFE penalty.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For periodic cross-border payments to overseas equipment suppliers, logistics, insurance, and marketing vendors, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 against a true trade invoice and contract, with submission through the bank's FX settlement system and SAFE goods-trade reporting. For bulk procurement of camping equipment or raw materials, irrevocable sight or usance commercial letters of credit are appropriate when a supplier requires title document safeguards. For lower-value recurring shipments, documentary collections with bills of lading and inspection certificates offer a cleaner mismatch control. All outbound disbursements must be supported by valid trade documentation and reported to SAFE within 30 days, with annual total amounts consistent with the WFOE's business scope.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts executed with a licensed domestic bank on genuine current account exposure
FX swaps between CNY and USD for short-term liquidity management of trade payables and receivables
Vanilla currency options and collars sold or granted by licensed onshore banks under true-exposure verification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' Annual General Meeting Resolutions and Meeting Minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Central Regional Commercial Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entities, the AGM must be convened on or before 30 June of the following fiscal year; minutes of resolutions must be filed with the registration authority within 15 days after the meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of TWD 20,000–100,000; subsequent failure to rectify after formal notice may lead to the revocation of company registration and compulsory strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (certified by an independent CPA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Central Regional Commercial Registration Office; Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission (for foreign-invested WFOE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be submitted within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, on or before 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of TWD 20,000–100,000 under the Company Act; persistent non-compliance may invalidate foreign investment approval and expose the entity to administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Report and updated Shareholders' Register (Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (on or before 30 June for calendar-year companies), accompanied by audited financial statements and a capital/shareholding reconciliation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of TWD 60,000–300,000 under the Investment Regulations; prolonged non-reporting can result in suspension of foreign exchange privileges and revocation of the WFOE investment permit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register Annual Verification and Change Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration Online System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The UBO register must be audited and updated at the AGM; any change in directors, controlling shareholders, or beneficial owners must be filed with MOEA within 15 days of the triggering event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of TWD 10,000–100,000 for failure to maintain accurate UBO data; material inaccuracies or repeated non-filing may trigger an official warning followed by strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A WFOE in Taiwan is categorically required to have its annual financial statements audited and certified by an independent certified public accountant due to foreign investment status; additionally, non-public companies with paid-in capital of TWD 30 million or more are subject to mandatory statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TW FRS) which are fully converged with IFRS; for smaller non-public entities, the same framework applies as the WFOE must file audited statements with the Investment Commission under Taiwan local GAAP/TW FRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the WFOE must maintain a register of directors, controlling shareholders, major shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners. The register is updated annually at the AGM date, and any share transfer or ownership change must be reconciled and electronically declared to MOEA within 15 days. An annual standalone UBO declaration is not required if no changes occurred, but the completed register must be available on-site and presented for inspection by the company secretary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders ledger with share certificates and transfer records)
Register of Directors (including supervisors and beneficial owner declarations)
Minute Book (AGM and board meeting minutes)
Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO register required under Company Act Article 22-1)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for online retail; effective rate is reduced through a 10-year loss carryforward (with certified accounting records), R&D and smart-industry investment tax credits under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, and arm's-length expense deductibility; undistributed profits exceeding permitted reserves are subject to an additional 5% retained-earnings surtax under Article 66-9 of the Income Tax Act, increasing the burden on retained profits.
